In 25 patients, 67 stimulations across 128 insular sites gave a response (Afif 2010).

regions.driven: In 329 patients (1,789 cingulate sites; 50 Hz, 1 ms, 5 s, 2.7 ± 0.7 mA), the posterior cingulate was poorly excitable but was the main source of visual effects; the caudal midcingulate gave most vestibular responses (Caruana 2018). In one patient, intra-operative stimulation disrupting PCC connections caused brief unresponsiveness and a dream-like disconnection (Herbet 2014).

regions.name: Anterior cingulate cortex (pregenual/subgenual)
regions.anatomy: Brainnetome pregenual A32p (published centre -6,34,21); closest voxel 34.4 mm; 10-5 AFF1h 47.7 mm. Subgenual A32sg (-4,39,-2) 46.7 mm (Fpz 49.6). HO cingulate anterior division (-4.5,17.7,24.6) 55.7 mm, closest 39.6 mm. Neurosynth 'anterior cingulate' L (-4,34,20) 46.9 mm. sgACC anticorrelation is the basis of Fox 2012 DLPFC targeting.
regions.function: Conflict monitoring, emotion regulation (pgACC/sgACC), autonomic control; sgACC implicated in depression
regions.driven: Across 1,789 cingulate sites in 329 patients (50 Hz, 1 ms, 5 s, 2.7 ± 0.7 mA), 32.3 % responded; pregenual sites gave emotional, interoceptive and autonomic responses, anterior midcingulate sites goal-directed actions (Caruana 2018). Pregenual stimulation caused laughter in 10 patients, half with mirth (Caruana 2015). Felt intensity rose with current across 1–8 mA (Yih 2019), and 2 patients described a 'will to persevere' (Parvizi 2013).

regions.name: Caudate nucleus
regions.anatomy: HO left caudate centroid; closest voxel 51.7 mm; 10-5 FFC5 64.8 mm; F5 65.1 mm. Right (13.3,10.1,10.4) 62.3 mm (F6h). Neurosynth 'caudate' L (-8,10,4) 66.6 mm. Single-coil |B| ~0.18 µT (F7/FT7).
regions.function: Goal-directed action selection, reward learning, cognitive control loops
regions.murphy: Caudate: 'emotive-visceral integrator', left = arousal, right = relaxation ('preliminary reports'). Septum: 'pleasure center', orgasm centres ('four for women and one for men'). Thalamus: 'pacemaker', dreamless-sleep states.
regions.driven: No human direct-stimulation or TMS report of subjective effects from the caudate nucleus was found in this research.

regions.name: Putamen
regions.anatomy: HO left putamen centroid; closest voxel 46.6 mm; 10-5 FT7h 57.8 mm; FT7 58.7 mm. Right (25.5,1.8,0.3) 54.0 mm. Neurosynth 'putamen' L (-26,2,8) 51.9 mm. Single-coil |B|: FT7 0.32 µT.
regions.function: Motor/habit loops, sensorimotor learning
regions.driven: No human direct-stimulation or TMS report of subjective effects from the putamen was found in this research.

regions.name: Thalamus
regions.anatomy: HO left thalamus centroid; closest voxel 59.7 mm; 10-5 T7h 73.4 mm; C5 74.3 mm. Right (10.8,-18.3,6.7) 72.9 mm. Neurosynth 'thalamus' L (-10,-18,2) 71.8 mm. Single-coil |B| ~0.14 µT; layout B in phase ~0.21 µT.
regions.function: Relay and gating of sensory/motor information, arousal, cortico-thalamic rhythms
regions.murphy: Caudate: 'emotive-visceral integrator', left = arousal, right = relaxation ('preliminary reports'). Septum: 'pleasure center', orgasm centres ('four for women and one for men'). Thalamus: 'pacemaker', dreamless-sleep states.
regions.driven: A review of stimulation reports notes that thalamic stimulation disrupted verbal and non-verbal memory processing (Selimbeyoglu & Parvizi 2010).

regions.name: Left DLPFC (TMS depression target)
regions.anatomy: Fox 2012 efficacy-optimised coordinate (also Mir-Moghtadaei 2015 target); nearest 10-5 F5h/F3 22 mm. Other definitions: Fox sgACC-optimised (-44,38,34) 14.1 mm (F3 18 mm); Rajkowska BA46 (-44,40,29) 14.9 mm; BA9 (-36,39,43) 15.0 mm; 5 cm rule average (-41,16,54) 15.7 mm (FC3); Brainnetome A9/46d (-27,43,31) 24.5 mm, A9/46v (-41,41,16) 21.0 mm, A46 (-28,56,12) 21.1 mm; Neurosynth 'dlpfc' L (-46,38,30) 14.0 mm; Dan lab F3 cortical projection (-39.8,44.3,31.7) MFG BA46 76%.
regions.function: Working memory and executive control; rTMS antidepressant target (efficacy related to sgACC anticorrelation)
regions.driven: Direct stimulation of lateral prefrontal cortex yields only isolated case reports, such as dream-like visual experiences at 5–10 mA in the left middle/inferior frontal gyrus (Blanke 2000, cited by Raccah 2021). TMS here gives no acute percept; a 301-patient depression trial used 10 Hz rTMS at 120 % of motor threshold, 5 days a week for 4–6 weeks (O'Reardon 2007). Motor-threshold TMS induces about 96–179 V/m here (Turi 2022 models).

regions.name: Right DLPFC
regions.anatomy: Neurosynth 'dlpfc' right association peak; nearest 10-5 F4 19 mm, F6h 20 mm. Brainnetome A9/46d R (30,37,36) 25.5 mm (F4 28.2). Dan lab F4 cortical projection (42.4,43.6,33.1) MFG BA46 76%.
regions.function: Executive control, inhibition; low-frequency rTMS target in some depression protocols
regions.driven: Direct stimulation of lateral prefrontal cortex yields only isolated case reports (Raccah 2021). TMS gives no acute percept; motor-threshold TMS induces about 96–179 V/m at the DLPFC in head models (Turi 2022). The 301-patient depression trial of 10 Hz rTMS targeted the left DLPFC, not this side (O'Reardon 2007).

regions.name: vmPFC / medial orbitofrontal cortex
regions.anatomy: HO frontal medial cortex (left half); closest voxel 30.4 mm; 10-5 Fp1h 47.0 mm; Fpz 48.0 mm. Brainnetome medial A11 (-6,52,-19) 35.2 mm, medial A14 (-7,54,-7) 32.6 mm. Neurosynth 'vmpfc' L (-4,44,-10) 42.4 mm; R (4,58,-4) 28.1 mm. Coils at Fpz/Fp1/Fp2 sit over the frontal sinus/forehead; best approach is Fp1h/Fpz.
regions.function: Valuation, emotion regulation, self-referential and default-mode processing
regions.driven: Direct stimulation here is almost entirely silent: across 1,537 sites in 67 patients (50 Hz, 2–10 mA), effects were 'almost entirely absent in the core of the medial prefrontal cortex' (Fox 2020). A later review adds that anterior prefrontal stimulation 'almost never affects conscious experience', and cites a null series of 36 patients (Trevisi 2018, via Raccah 2021).

regions.name: Lateral orbitofrontal cortex
regions.anatomy: HO frontal orbital cortex (left half); closest voxel 17.1 mm; F7 45.2 mm. Right (29.1,23.1,-16.2) 44.2 mm (F8). Neurosynth 'orbitofrontal' L (-22,34,-16) 43.8 mm.
regions.function: Outcome valuation, reversal learning, olfactory/gustatory integration
regions.driven: In 22 patients (50 Hz, 2–8 mA), 30 of 172 orbitofrontal sites (17.4 %) gave effects: smell 13, body sensation 8, taste 3, smell and taste 3, negative emotion 2. Sites at y ≤ 40 mm responded 20.4 % of the time, sites further forward only 2.5 % (Fox 2018). In another series, 75 % of OFC stimulation effects involved smell or taste (Yih 2019).

regions.name: Primary visual cortex (V1, BA17)
regions.anatomy: Juelich V1 (left) centroid; closest voxel 8.6 mm (V1 reaches the occipital pole surface); 10-5 O1h 31.3 mm; Oz 32.6 mm. Right V1 (13.3,-82.4,3.3) 35.0 mm (O2). Most of V1 lies in the calcarine sulcus. Neurosynth 'v1' L (-4,-90,-2) 29.4 mm; R (10,-94,2) 24.3 mm. Dan lab: O1/O2/Oz projections BA17 96-100%. Single-coil |B| at centroid: Oz 0.96 µT (ring).
regions.function: Primary visual processing; magnetophosphene/visual-percept reports would most plausibly involve retina/occipital cortex
regions.murphy: Simple visual phenomena, visual acuity; remote viewing (proposed, untested).
regions.driven: Direct stimulation reliably produced phosphenes at 0.2–5 mA (5–100 Hz, 200–1,000 µs pulses), activating up to about 1 cm² of cortex; phosphene ratings rose from 1–2 below 10 µC to 9–10 above 100 µC, and 13 sham trials gave no false positives (Winawer & Parvizi 2016). TMS with a figure-of-eight coil over the inion evoked phosphenes in 10 of 10 subjects (Kammer 1999).

regions.name: Fusiform gyrus
regions.anatomy: Neurosynth 'fusiform' left peak (right peak (42,-50,-20) 36.7 mm); nearest 10-5 TPP9h 40 mm, P9h 41 mm. HO temporal-occipital fusiform L (-33.5,-53.7,-16.0) 43.2 mm, closest 27.1 mm (P7 45.7); Brainnetome lateroventral A37 (-42,-50,-17) 36.2 mm, medioventral A37 (-31,-64,-14) 39.8 mm.
regions.function: High-level visual recognition (faces, words, objects)
regions.driven: Stimulating right fusiform face patches at 2–4 mA (mostly 3 mA; 50 Hz, 200 µs, about 1 s) distorted a viewed face ('Your face metamorphosed'); sham trials and contacts 1.7 cm more medial changed nothing (Parvizi 2012). Only right fusiform stimulation changed face perception; left fusiform stimulation gave non-face effects such as phosphenes (Rangarajan 2014).

regions.name: Left cerebellum Crus I
regions.depthNote: distance from the nearest scalp site to the nearest tissue
regions.function: Lateral posterior cerebellar cortex (Diedrichsen 2009 label 8). Meta-analytic association at the centroid (Neurosynth): cerebellum, lobule VI, sensorimotor network.
regions.driven: TMS over the cerebellum (not Crus I specifically) suppressed motor-cortex responses at 5–7 ms intervals, with no percept reported (Ugawa 1995). In 12 volunteers, 20 min of 1 Hz cerebellar rTMS caused no mood change right after, but more negative mood after an emotion-regulation task (Schutter & van Honk 2009). No human direct-stimulation data for Crus I were found.

contralateral.name: Right cerebellum Crus I
contralateral.anatomy: Nearest-tissue distances: P10 23.4 mm, PO10 25.7 mm, TP10 30.3 mm.

regions.name: Cerebellum Crus II (left and right)
regions.depthNote: distance from the nearest scalp site to the nearest tissue
regions.function: Posterior-inferior cerebellar cortex (Diedrichsen 2009 labels 11 and 13). Meta-analytic association at the left centroid (Neurosynth): lobule VI, cerebellar lobules, theory of mind, timing.
regions.driven: No human direct-stimulation or TMS data specific to Crus II were found. General cerebellar TMS findings (motor-cortex inhibition, no reported percept) are listed under Crus I.
regions.terms: lobule VI, lobules, theory of mind, timing

contralateral.name: Right cerebellum Crus II
contralateral.anatomy: Nearest-tissue distances: I2 27.9 mm, Iz 29.6 mm.

regions.name: Cerebellar vermis VI (with dentate nuclei)
regions.depthNote: distance from the nearest scalp site to the nearest tissue
regions.function: Midline cerebellar cortex (vermis lobule VI, Diedrichsen 2009 label 6); the dentate nuclei (labels 29 and 30) lie deeper on each side. Meta-analytic association (Neurosynth): vermis and movement at vermis VI; 'nuclei' at the dentate.
regions.driven: Open-label vermal theta-burst TMS (10 sessions, 8 patients with schizophrenia) was followed by mood elevation and fewer negative symptoms; side effects were neck pain and headache (Demirtas-Tatlidede 2010).

markers.name: Left dentate nucleus
markers.depthNote: nearest tissue; centroid 57.1 mm from PO9

markers.name: Right dentate nucleus
markers.depthNote: only the centroid distance was given: 59.0 mm from POO10

regions.name: Brainstem (midbrain PAG marker)
regions.depthNote: depth to the nearest brainstem tissue; the point shown is the periaqueductal grey, about 84 mm from the nearest site
regions.function: Midbrain, pons and medulla (FreeSurfer aseg label 16, 31 cm³). The marker is a periaqueductal grey (PAG) point used as a Neurosynth query; substantia nigra and other midbrain nuclei come from CIT168. Meta-analytic association at the PAG point (Neurosynth): periaqueductal, brainstem, pain.
regions.driven: Stereotactic stimulation of the dorsal and periaqueductal midbrain gave somatosensory, ocular, emotional and vasomotor responses, organised by body part (Iacono & Nashold 1982). In one Parkinson's patient, high-frequency deep brain stimulation that reached the left substantia nigra, 2 mm below the effective subthalamic contact, caused transient acute depression (Bejjani 1999).

zones.name: Left temporal lobe – 4-coil cross (God Helmet / 8 Coil Shakti)
zones.anatomy: Lateral temporal cortex (superior and middle temporal gyri) over the left mesial temporal lobe. Translation from 'about an inch above each ear' and the vendor's 'cross' chart is an inference.
zones.claimed: Murphy: left amygdala = positive emotion (joy, elation, bliss, 'meaningfulness'); left hippocampus = verbal and logical thought, but 'negative thoughts', irritability; target for amygdala-left phases.

zones.name: Right temporal lobe – 4-coil cross
zones.anatomy: Right lateral temporal cortex over the right mesial temporal lobe (inference).
zones.claimed: Murphy: right hippocampus = non-verbal cognition, imagery, music, intuition, 'peace', dreams (target for hippocampus-right phases); right amygdala = fear and sadness (phase-1 fear in the classic design).
zones.mainstream: Persinger-lab only: LTP-pattern fields rated more pleasant over the right (1994); burst-firing over the right raised apprehension in women (1992).

zones.name: Shiva / Octopus circumcerebral ring
zones.anatomy: A horizontal ring on the 10% circumference, avoiding the nasion, inion and pre-auricular (T7/T8) points per Murphy's rules; lab: 'temporo-orbital plane' / 'horizontal plane above the ears'.
zones.claimed: Deflect a 25 ms front-to-back '40 Hz binding factor'; counter-clockwise favours the right hemisphere; theta enhancement; psi.
zones.mainstream: Persinger lab: about 30% theta increase (Richards 2002); hemisphere bias by rotation direction (Booth 2008). Not independently replicated.

zones.name: Frontal lobes (bilateral) – Feelgood / reset sessions
zones.anatomy: Prefrontal cortex ('one coil over each eye'; translation is an inference).
zones.claimed: Mood lift, 'forward-looking', 'this-worldly'; frontal sessions 'can undo the effects of temporal lobe sessions, and vice versa'; right frontal = possible precognition (speculative).
zones.mainstream: Persinger lab: left-frontal or bilateral-temporal burst-firing both reduced post-TBI depression (Baker-Price 2003); left-prefrontal burst-firing raised acceptance of false statements (Ross 2008).

zones.name: Temporo-frontal area
zones.anatomy: Inferior frontal and anterior temporal cortex (inference).
zones.claimed: 'Language, mood, and relating to others'; left plus amygdala signal for people who feel bad in the morning; 'one of the best places to start' for one-sided use.

sources.title: Shakti demo: 8 Coil Shakti over the temporo-frontal area

zones.name: Parietal strip
zones.anatomy: Postcentral and superior parietal cortex: 'about an inch behind the topmost point on the head, and then in a strip down to the top of the ears' (translation is an inference).
zones.claimed: Body awareness; tingling and movement sensations; left = energised or irritable, right = relaxed or lethargic; caudate and amygdala signals.

zones.name: Top of parietal lobes (paracentral) – septal placement
zones.anatomy: Medial somatosensory cortex ('where the somatosensory representation for the genitals is located', per vendor).
zones.claimed: Septal ('pleasure center') signal for sexual sensation effects.

zones.name: Right angular gyrus / temporo-parieto-occipital junction
zones.anatomy: Right angular gyrus within the TPJ (10-10 translation approximate, my inference).
zones.claimed: OBE facilitation (with chirp, modulated 40 Hz, ERP or caudate); spatial perception; macropsia.
zones.mainstream: Focal electrical stimulation of the right angular gyrus repeatedly induced OBEs in one epilepsy patient (Blanke et al. 2002).

zones.name: Occipital lobes
zones.anatomy: Visual cortex 'above the bony ridge at the back of the head'.
zones.claimed: Simple visual phenomena, visual acuity; remote viewing (proposed, untested).
zones.mainstream: Persinger lab: occipital 7 Hz spike-and-slow-wave correlated with Swann's accuracy (rho = .50).

zones.name: Cerebellum (below inion)
zones.anatomy: Cerebellar vermis and hemispheres below the occipital ridge.
zones.claimed: 'Pleasure/orgasm' involvement; may mute the amygdala; ERP 'undo' site; risk of 'emotional flattening'.

siteGroups.driven: Stimulating the most anterior prefrontal cortex 'almost never affects conscious experience' (Raccah 2021). Orbitofrontal sites in front of y = 40 mm responded only 2.5 % of the time (Fox 2018).

rTMS up to 25 Hz over left fronto-temporal grid points gave reproducible speech arrest in 6 of 6 patients; right-side stimulation gave none (Pascual-Leone 1991). Matching their grid points to these 10-10 sites is the research's own inference.

In 13 patients, medial frontal stimulation below the afterdischarge threshold gave body-mapped complex movements, speech arrest and an 'urge' to move (Fried 1991). In one patient, stimulation of the left anterior SMA (superior frontal gyrus) gave laughter with mirth (Fried 1998).

TMS at resting motor threshold evokes hand muscle responses; head models put the field at 97.7–177 V/m in motor cortex at that threshold (Turi 2022). Direct stimulation gives body-mapped movement or sensation (Selimbeyoglu & Parvizi 2010 review).

In one patient, right angular gyrus stimulation gave vestibular sensations at 2.0–3.0 mA and an out-of-body experience at 3.5 mA (Blanke 2002); in another, left TPJ stimulation at 10–11 mA gave a 'shadow person' (Arzy 2006). Inferior parietal stimulation gave an intention to move (Desmurget 2009), and parietal operculum stimulation vestibular illusions (Kahane 2003).

Stimulating the cortex under these sites gave sounds and voices (Selimbeyoglu & Parvizi 2010) and, in mid to posterior STG/MTG, spinning vestibular illusions (Kahane 2003). Experiential phenomena (18 of 29 patients) occurred only when stimulation or a seizure involved limbic structures, which lie about 55 mm deep (Gloor 1982; Bancaud 1994). Penfield's experiential responses came from about 7 % of temporal stimulations (Nitsch & Stahnisch 2018).

Temporal-pole stimulation evoked voices, fear, sadness and happiness (Selimbeyoglu & Parvizi 2010 review); one 74-patient series counted fear at 6 contacts, mirth at 4 and sadness at 3 (Meletti 2006, via Hao 2023).

Temporo-occipital stimulation gave slowed-motion illusions and complex visual hallucinations such as people (Selimbeyoglu & Parvizi 2010 review). The fusiform gyrus lies about 38 mm below; stimulating its right face patches at 2–4 mA (mostly 3 mA) distorted faces (Parvizi 2012).
Direct stimulation of V1 produced phosphenes at 0.2–5 mA (Winawer & Parvizi 2016). TMS with a coil over the inion evoked phosphenes in 10 of 10 subjects (Kammer 1999).

Across 885 stimulations in 25 patients, stimulation inside the posteromedial cortex produced no observable or reported effect (Foster & Parvizi 2017). Older review tables list levitation and vertigo from dorsomedial parietal cortex (Selimbeyoglu & Parvizi 2010).

Cerebellar TMS suppressed motor-cortex responses at 5–7 ms intervals with no reported percept (Ugawa 1995). In 12 volunteers, 20 min of 1 Hz cerebellar rTMS changed mood only after an emotion-regulation task (Schutter & van Honk 2009).
siteGroups.anatomy: Nearest cerebellar tissue: Crus I about 22–30 mm below P9/P10/TP9/TP10 (and PO10), Crus II about 23–30 mm below PO9/I1/Iz/I2. The brainstem is about 64 mm or more away.

drivenSource: Direct electrical stimulation (DES) and TMS findings from the project research (brain-view track, fact-checked). They describe currents of milliamps or fields of about 100 V/m, not this helmet.
